clue.text: Come together on part of ship for a game

parts.note: to contract is to draw together or shrink
the bridge is the raised platform from which a ship is commanded

explanation.surface: An invitation to gather on deck for a round of something.
explanation.definitionFit: A card game for four players in partnerships, the standard modern form of bridge.

clue.text: Upbringing of awkward runt on river

indicators.note: in a down clue, on places the first piece above the second
awkward suggests the small word is clumsily put together in a different order

parts.note: the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: The rearing of a clumsy runt beside a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awkward' rearranges RUNT to NURT; the Ure is a river in North Yorkshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Nurture is the care and training given to a child as it grows, a synonym of upbringing.

clue.text: Cycle from a hill to the north

indicators.note: in a down entry, going to the north means reading upwards, backwards

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: Cycling away from a hill heading north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to the north' turns A TOR upwards to give the answer. 'Cycle' looks like riding a bike; it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A rota is a rotating schedule of duties, a recurring cycle.

clue.text: Bird observed at an angle

parts.note: a cock is a male bird
eyed means looked at, observed

explanation.surface: A bird spotted from a slanted viewpoint.
explanation.definitionFit: Cockeyed means askew or crooked, set on a slant.

clue.text: Contradicted old priest in Rose's place

indicators.note: in places the priest within the flower's place

parts.note: a rose grows in a flower bed
Eli is the Old Testament priest who taught Samuel

explanation.surface: A clergyman of old found contradicting Rose at her home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rose' looks like a woman's name; capitalised at the start of the phrase it is the flower.
explanation.definitionFit: To belie is to show something to be false, so the past tense means contradicted.

clue.text: It could bring one up to scratch

definitions.text: It could bring one up to scratch

parts.words: It could bring one up to scratch
parts.note: up to scratch usually means up to standard; here it is literal, an itch provoking scratching

explanation.surface: Something that might improve a person to an acceptable standard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up to scratch' looks like the idiom for satisfactory; read literally, something makes you start scratching.
explanation.definitionFit: Skin soreness or itching is what drives a person to scratch.

clue.text: Heartless girl in debt is full of praise

indicators.note: heartless means the middle of the word is removed

parts.note: owing means in debt

explanation.surface: A cold-hearted indebted girl who nonetheless gushes compliments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heartless' removes IR, the middle of GIRL, leaving GL.
explanation.definitionFit: A glowing report is warmly enthusiastic, full of praise.

clue.text: Suffer a hoax; it's an order

parts.note: to stand something is to put up with it
a tease is a joke played on someone, a hoax

explanation.surface: Putting up with a practical joke because you were told to.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a military command to soldiers to relax their posture.

clue.text: Fault-finding like one in an armchair perhaps

definitions.meaning: quick to point out faults, censorious

definitions.text: like one in an armchair perhaps
definitions.meaning: an armchair critic judges from comfort without taking part; being like a critic is this adjective's other sense

explanation.surface: A grumbler criticising everything from the comfort of an easy chair.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition leans on the phrase 'armchair critic': someone in an armchair perhaps is a critic, and the adjective means of or like a critic.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: censorious in tone, and pertaining to critics or criticism.

clue.text: Marsupial way beyond perch

indicators.note: beyond places the way after the marsupial in the answer

parts.note: roo is short for kangaroo, a marsupial
St is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: A kangaroo bounding down a road past a bird's perch.
explanation.definitionFit: A roost is a place where birds settle to rest, a synonym of a perch.

clue.text: Definitely important fruit coming from city?

parts.note: the is the definite article, so definitely points to it
big means important
an apple is a fruit

explanation.surface: Some significant fruit supposedly originating from a town.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition by example: New York's nickname.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the well-known nickname of New York City.

clue.text: Drag from anteroom as stated

indicators.note: as stated means as spoken, so the word for the room is heard rather than written

parts.note: a hall is an entrance room or lobby, an anteroom

explanation.surface: Someone dragging something out of a waiting room, as reported.
explanation.walkthrough: In non-rhotic British speech HALL and HAUL are pronounced alike.
explanation.definitionFit: To haul something is to pull or drag it with effort; a verb synonym.

clue.text: Train speed somehow not very fast

indicators.note: somehow suggests the letters are put together in some unspecified new order

explanation.surface: A complaint that a train is crawling along.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somehow' rearranges TRAIN SPEED. 'Train' looks like the subject; it is only fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A walker moves at walking pace, so on foot means not very fast; it also means dull and plodding.

clue.text: Saving claim one prepared about small company

indicators.note: about places the rearranged words around the company
prepared suggests the words are worked up into a new arrangement

parts.note: Co is the short form of company

explanation.surface: A firm's statement drawn up to save money for a little business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saving' reads as a noun in the surface; it is an adjective meaning thrifty. 'prepared' is the anagram signal and 'about' the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Economical describes thrift, using little; saving as an adjective.

clue.text: Paled, having lost blood with inner pain

indicators.note: with inner says the second piece sits on the inside of the first

parts.note: bled means lost blood
an ache is a pain

explanation.surface: Someone going white after bleeding and in pain.
explanation.definitionFit: Bleached means whitened or lost colour, as a face does when it pales.

clue.text: Greek character taking time to make mark

indicators.note: taking means the Greek letter takes in, holds, the other piece

parts.note: sigma is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A Greek person needing time to leave their mark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'character' looks like a person in the surface; here it is a letter of an alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: A stigma is a mark of disgrace, and also literally a visible mark or spot.

clue.text: Supporter fills in test for part of the army

indicators.note: fills means the supporter goes into the gap of the other pieces

parts.note: a try is a test or attempt
a fan is a supporter

explanation.surface: A sports supporter sitting an exam to get into the army.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fills' signals the container: the supporter goes into the gap between the two other pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Foot soldiers form one branch of the army.

clue.text: Gritty? It is not clear

definitions.meaning: said of a photograph or picture blurred by visible graininess

explanation.surface: Asking whether something is gritty, and admitting nobody can tell.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both coarse granular texture and a blurred, speckled image.

clue.text: Scored briskly?

parts.note: scored looks like a sporting term; here it means written in a musical score, with a fast tempo marking

explanation.surface: Points racked up at speed.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the Italian tempo marking telling musicians to play quickly and lively.

clue.text: Separate a continental pair

parts.note: un is French for a, so a European on the continent would say it
a couple is a pair

explanation.surface: A command to split up a European couple.
explanation.definitionFit: To uncouple is to detach or disconnect, as railway wagons are separated.

clue.text: Moved camera round left as intended

indicators.note: round says the camera movement goes around the left

parts.note: to pan is to swing a camera across a scene

explanation.surface: A cameraman swinging round to the left as the script said.
explanation.definitionFit: Planned means arranged in advance, so it happened as intended.

clue.text: 'No way out' admits husband, carelessly

indicators.note: admits says the rearranged words let in the husband
out means the words are put out of their order

explanation.surface: A husband concedes there is no escape, sounding off without care.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges NO WAY to ANYOW, and 'admits' takes in H.
explanation.definitionFit: Done in any old way means done haphazardly, without care.

clue.text: Fellow with endless fish getting behind tug for carriage

indicators.note: getting behind puts the fellow and fish after the tug in the answer

parts.note: a tug is a pull
a fellow is a man

indicators.note: endless means the fish loses its final letter

parts.note: carp is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: A man with a fish towed along behind a tugboat.
explanation.definitionFit: A Pullman is a luxurious railway carriage, named after its American designer.

clue.text: Second-rate fool and singer?

parts.note: B is the grade below A, second-rate
an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: Calling a vocalist a mediocre idiot.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the definition by example: a bass is one kind of singer.
explanation.definitionFit: A bass is a male singer with the lowest vocal range.

clue.text: What's worn part of brake?

definitions.meaning: the curved block pressing against a wheel or drum in a braking system

explanation.surface: Asking which component of a brake is worn down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worn' suggests wear and tear on the brake; it is simply clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both footwear and the friction block of a drum brake.

clue.text: 99th record? It stands to reason

parts.note: a log is a written record, as of a voyage
IC is 99 in Roman numerals, read here as the numeral that follows

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a ninety-ninth record is inevitable.
explanation.walkthrough: The record comes before the 99 in the answer: Roman numerals IC = 100 minus 1.
explanation.definitionFit: Reasoning is what this discipline studies, and what stands to reason is what follows by sound argument.

clue.text: Some shady work coming out of an egg

definitions.meaning: fine parallel lines used to shade a drawing
emerging from the shell, as a chick does

explanation.surface: Something dodgy being plotted, like a scheme emerging from its shell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shady' suggests dishonesty; it is literal shading in drawing.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both line-shading in art and a chick breaking out of its shell.

clue.text: Understand article I have written for game

parts.note: to follow an argument is to understand it
what I have is mine, my
a leader is a newspaper's main editorial article

explanation.surface: A journalist asking readers to grasp the editorial they wrote for a match.
explanation.walkthrough: A leader is the British term for a newspaper editorial; 'written' is a link reinforcing the newspaper picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A children's game in which everyone copies whatever the person in front does.
